reasoning: Both sets plan all six stages in full, hand-write the core algorithms before comparing them with libraries, and send every beats-chance claim to the null-hypothesis-testing skill by name at the step where the test happens. A's set is stronger on quant substance. It records exit values and delisting returns instead of ending at the last traded price. It has a known-truth synthetic test bed for the estimators and for HRP's robustness claim, a null test bed matched to feature persistence with a power table, and a pre-registered registry with BH exploration followed by a single Holm confirmation. Its Stage 5 and Stage 6 claims are explicitly relative, backed by prospective logs, and its PPO meta-allocator is checked on a known-answer environment against non-RL selectors. B has good ideas too: a log of tries with Holm across every attempt, sequential single-use holdouts, a sealed paper period and guardrail gates. But it has real defects. Its 200-draw incremental null cannot reach Holm thresholds near 0.0017, so GATE-03 and every INCR claim are blocked. Delisting payouts are not modeled. Its out-of-scope list still excludes 'deep learning' and 'Machine-learning portfolio methods', which contradicts Stages 5 and 6. HOLD-06 says no study reads 2025+ data, yet the Stage 2/3 walk-forward runs to the last complete month. It also keeps residue: a superseded AD-19 stub, a merged idea stub, about 15 '(changed 2026-10-15)' tags and a stale 'two holdouts' in AD-20. A has its own stale bits: a 'Merged into Goal 2' placeholder, a Holm-only assumption that contradicts SIG-01's BH families, 'Milestone-1' notebook references and outdated run-folder headings. It is also heavier to read. Neither set has a global next-step roadmap. On balance A's content is more sound and more consistent, and the two are about equal on structure.

Known-truth synthetic test bed (SYN) for estimators and for HRP's robustness claim, plus a pure-noise null test bed matched to feature persistence with a planted-signal power table (CALIB)
Pre-registered, hashed feature registry; BH exploration then a single Holm-corrected confirmatory test on a locked 3-year holdout that can be opened only once
Every test family is named in SIG-01 and in each requirement, with an explicit tests.json/results.json file contract to the null-hypothesis-testing skill; eqdata never computes its own p-values
Stage 5 and 6 claims are explicitly relative because holdout years are already used, confirmed by 12- and 24-month prospective hash-chained logs

PPO meta-allocator validated on Pendulum and on a two-regime environment with an exactly computed optimum, against Stable-Baselines3 and two non-RL selectors; MVO uses IC x vol x score with a reported shrinkage path
Worked numeric examples check out (RET-01 returns, VOL-01 proxy 0.000407, PORT-12 34/22 tests, CONF-02 62 tests, FCST-04 54 tests, BENCH-03 26 tests)

Guardrail gates per stage (GATE placebo, relabel and planted signal; FGATE simulated GARCH and planted interaction; SGATE replication, random and oracle allocators)
The baseline is chosen per fold on training data (best of EWMA/GARCH/HAR, best classical portfolio), so one tested claim per candidate keeps families small
PPO trained on block-bootstrapped histories rather than the single real path; per-stock PPO and the simulation study are parked rather than bloating scope
